standard.title: Plan statistical investigations
standard.description: Plan and conduct statistical investigations by posing questions or identifying a problem and collecting relevant data; choose appropriate displays and interpret the data; communicate findings within the context of the investigation
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can conduct statistical investigations with guidance (AC9M4ST03). They have not yet planned the full investigation cycle independently, including posing their own question and selecting displays.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students plan and conduct statistical investigations, posing questions, collecting and displaying data, interpreting findings and communicating conclusions.

nodes.label: Posing an investigative question
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can pose a statistical question that can be answered with data, distinguishing it from a question with a single certain answer.
nodes.minimum_width: Pose a statistical question about a given topic; explain why it requires data to answer.
nodes.typical_width: Pose and refine statistical questions; distinguish statistical questions from fixed-answer questions; connect the question to the data that would answer it.
wider: Compare statistical and causal questions: what can statistics answer vs what requires experiment?
Investigate how survey questions are designed to be statistical

response_modes.reason: The distinction between a statistical question and a fixed-answer question requires an explicit reasoning scaffold: 'what data would I need?' and 'would different samples give different answers?' Students who skip this step design uncollectable investigations.

nodes.hinge_reason: A poorly posed question cannot be answered by data — students who cannot distinguish statistical from fixed-answer questions produce investigations with no collectible data, collapsing every subsequent phase (Mode B phase collapse).
success_criteria: Student poses a question that requires data to answer
Student explains why the question is statistical (variability in answers expected)

nodes.label: Collecting and displaying data
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can collect data relevant to their question and choose and construct an appropriate display.
nodes.minimum_width: Collect data for a posed question; create an appropriate display for the variable type.
nodes.typical_width: Design a data collection method; collect, validate and organise data; select and justify display type; construct the display accurately using software.
wider: Compare multiple display options for the same data and justify the best choice
Use online datasets to investigate questions beyond what class collection can answer
success_criteria: Student collects data relevant to their question using a systematic method
Student constructs an appropriate display for their variable type

nodes.label: Interpreting and communicating findings
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can interpret their data display and communicate findings within the context of their investigation.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe the main finding from their display; relate the finding back to the original question.
nodes.typical_width: Interpret the display for patterns, trends or comparisons; make conclusions supported by data; communicate findings using statistical language in a written or oral report.
wider: Critique an investigation design and suggest improvements
Present findings to an authentic audience (class, school community)

response_modes.reason: Communication of findings requires the full investigation cycle — posing, collecting, displaying, interpreting — to cohere into a coherent response to the original question. This is the Mode B assessment point where capability is visible through the work.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Authentic audience presentation and investigation critique are rich, purposeful tasks for advancing students.
success_criteria: Student relates findings to the original question
Student communicates at least one conclusion supported by data evidence
